source.title: Multi-Level Safety Continual Projection for Fine-Tuned Large Language Models without Retraining
source.authors: Bing Han; Fei-Fei Zhao; Dong-Cheng Zhao; Guo-Bin Shen; Ping Wu; Yu Shi; Yi Zeng

record.tranche_reason: The study edits a selected sparse set of safety-related weights and reports harmfulness outcomes, bearing on whether targeted parameters can affect safety behavior. It uses a different method from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work for safety degradation after harmful or benign fine-tuning but does not test those claims against an un-fine-tuned reference. Its results concern its own post-fine-tuning projection method; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes MSCP, a training-free defense that moves selected neurons in LoRA-finetuned models toward a base→aligned 'safety direction'. Every reported result is its own method's harmfulness or ASR against the LoRA-finetuned model and competing defenses. It cites Qi et al. for fine-tuning degradation but never measures safety before fine-tuning, so V2 is not tested. The neuron editing is a mitigation tool. It does not test whether a small parameter set carries safety: there is no ablation of those weights removing safety, and no necessity or sufficiency test. So the results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that MSCP identifies sparse safety-governing neuron clusters and, via training-free projections, cuts harmfulness and ASR with minimal edits and negligible utility loss. It also supports continual adaptation to new safety dimensions; broader continual learning needs further study.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies a training-free, post-fine-tuning projection to selected safety-neuron weights; it does not reproduce harmful or benign fine-tuning experiments or measure token-position KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety results depend on selected layer interval: the paper reports no significant reduction for shallow intervals and failure of late-stage intervention; layers 10–15 perform best. It states that Qwen shows consistent results but gives no corresponding numerical values in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity between benign and harmful hidden states diverges most between base and aligned Llama-3.1-8B at layers 10–15 (Fig. 2a–b). The finding is qualitative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment's representational change on harmful prompts concentrates in middle layers (layer-depth localization).

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting about 5% of LoRA parameters toward the base→aligned direction restores low harmfulness after benign LoRA fine-tuning (Tables 1–2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse post-hoc edits can restore safety eroded by fine-tuning.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The results evaluate the authors' own projection method and do not isolate whether the selected parameters are necessary or sufficient for safety behavior. Some layer-ablation findings are described qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: Other methods in Tables 1 and 2 were not included because they are comparison methods rather than results of the study's targeted sparse projection. Continual-dimension table results were not extracted because they do not test whether safety behavior is localized in a small parameter subset.

untested.parts: Benign Alpaca/GSM8K LoRA models show nonzero ASR (55%, 58%), but no pre-fine-tuning reference is reported.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No ablation or isolation showing a small weight set carries safety; only a restoration edit.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from T2/tests to T4/uses_without_test: this is a defense-method paper reporting only its own performance, and the reader's V5 labels are removed. The rows are internally inconsistent in naming Llama-3-8B-Instruct (tables) versus Llama3.1-8B-Instruct (text). The text states Qwen ablation results are 'consistent' but gives no numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison establishing that benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding intervention.
The study evaluates its selected sparse projections, but does not establish that the same small parameter subset is necessary or sufficient for safety across other edits or settings.
No test of whether the data or training objective produces safety shallowness.
No training that spreads safety across response tokens, nor test of such safety's durability.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The study reports safety improvements after editing 4.67%–5.46% of parameters; see r1–r12.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported safety effect depends on layer placement: shallow and late intervals fail to reduce the measures, while layers 10–15 perform best; see r13–r16.
